profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.East Building 1, sits on the Intergate.East sub-campus. Aggregator DatacenterHawk lists specific, distinct street numbers for neighboring Buildings 2 (3311), 3 (3333), and 5 (3355) within the shared address range, but no distinct number specific to Building 1 has been located in sourcing to date; the campus range is applied here instead rather than a guessed figure.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: Sabey publishes SDC Seattle only as a campus-wide total (1M+ sqft / 54MW across Intergate.East + Intergate.West sub-campuses), not broken out per building. No per-building figure exists for Intergate.East Building 1. No numeric key written.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle East Building 1 sits on the Intergate.East sub-campus of SDC Seattle in Tukwila, King County, Washington, one of seven Sabey data center campuses nationally totaling nearly 400 MW. The Tukwila campus as a whole publishes 54 MW of capacity across more than a million square feet, but the operator does not break this figure out per individual building, so the capacity of this specific building is not published. This campus ranks third by published MW in Washington state, which has only two facilities with operator-disclosed capacity figures totaling 60 MW.

Intergate.East spans roughly 1.2 million square feet across multiple buildings within a street range on South 120th Place. Building-specific power allocations are not disclosed, so any estimate of IT load must be derived from the full campus figure. As an assumption, if the 54 MW campus figure represents typical AI colocation density of roughly 40 kW per rack, the entire Intergate.East and Intergate.West sub-campuses would support approximately 1,350 racks; actual density varies widely by tenant class and workload.

No certifications, power purchase agreements, or grid-level constraints specific to this building are published in available operator materials. The Sabey Tukwila location traces to 1972 and entered the data center business during the dot-com collapse, but neither the vintage nor the operational history, nor details of power sourcing or current tenant mix, appear in the published specifications reviewed here.
